defectsFound.defect: The database projectone_dev did not exist. sys.databases held only master, model, msdb and tempdb. Canonical Step 99 configured the local development database CONNECTION; nothing ever created the database itself.
defectsFound.symptom: pyodbc.InterfaceError reporting 'Login failed for user' — misleading. The operative error was 4060, 'Cannot open database projectone_dev requested by the login'. SQL Server reports a login failure when it cannot open the requested database, so the message points at authentication when the cause is a missing database.
defectsFound.fix: CREATE DATABASE projectone_dev — empty, no schema. Environment setup, not implementation; clear of the Step 112 gate.
defectsFound.latency: Latent since Step 99. Invisible until the connection was exercised end to end, because configuring a connection string never touches the server.

defectsFound.defect: The 999 overlay register created at canonical Step 108 claimed to supersede the external 999-Agent-Build-Canon-Modification-Tracker-v0.4.md while containing only OV-001 and OV-002. That tracker held 27 APPROVED entries. None had been migrated.
defectsFound.howItHappened: The register was authored without access to the external tracker. The gap WAS flagged at the time as NOT_EXAMINED in PR #11's evidence section, so it was not a silent miss — but the header's supersedes claim was written as though complete, and stood untrue for six days.
defectsFound.whyItMattered: A register that looks complete is more dangerous than one that is obviously partial. A reader checking 'are there overlays on the DDR?' would have found none and concluded correctly from a false premise.
defectsFound.fix: All 27 entries migrated verbatim with original approvals; supersedes claim corrected; register v1.0 -> v2.0.
defectsFound.foundBy: Owner. John directed a double-check of whether prior DDR change proposals had been evaluated.
defectsFound.lesson: A NOT_EXAMINED note protects honesty but does not protect the artifact. When a claim depends on something unexamined, weaken the CLAIM, do not merely footnote it.

defectsFound.defect: The source registry stated the overlay rule — 'Effective source = immutable source + all applicable approved overlay entries. Reading the base source alone is an incomplete read.' — and provided an overlayRefs field on all 40 sources. ALL 40 WERE EMPTY. Separately, ROLE_CODING declared four source classes MANDATORY (GOVERNANCE_POLICY, DESIGN_RECORD, CONTRACT_REGISTRY, TECHNOLOGY_REGISTRY) and NONE were bound to files. Source 406 carried two approved overlays while absent from the registry entirely.
defectsFound.consequence: A coding agent was instructed to load the design record with nothing resolving that to a file, and a reader of the DDR had no way to learn that three approved decisions existed only as overlays. This is the mechanism behind CF-005, not a separate problem.
defectsFound.fix: overlayRefs populated on 14 sources from the register mechanically; readRule warning added to each; 406 and the Build Constraints Guide registered; sourceBundleBindings added binding all five classes; check_overlay_reachability.py built, negative-tested and made the 9th required status check.
defectsFound.foundBy: Owner. John asked where the principles should live for AI to read them with least risk of losing the authority.
defectsFound.lesson: A rule stated in a document and a field provided for it are not the same as the field being populated. Check the data, not the schema.

defectsFound.defect: The pilot dataset's SHA-256 was recorded in the snapshot as evidence of determinism. It was the hash of a file that did not exist in the repository. Python's csv module writes CRLF by default; .gitattributes normalises text to LF; so the generator produced CRLF, git stored LF, and the recorded hash matched neither the committed file nor anything a reader could reproduce.
defectsFound.whyItMattered: The CONTENT was never wrong — only the claim about it. That is the more dangerous failure: a hash recorded as evidence, proving nothing, that nobody would question because it looks like rigour.
defectsFound.fix: Generator writes LF explicitly; recorded hash corrected to 53707b90...; check_generated_data_reproducible.py built.
defectsFound.foundBy: A reproducibility comparison run during branch verification — regenerate and compare against the committed file. Not by any existing gate.
defectsFound.lesson: A recorded hash is only evidence if something re-derives it. Otherwise it is decoration that resembles proof.

findings: 402 Tracker: header reads v84; its own 'current canonical versions' line reads v82; the Manifest reads v80. Three values.
403 Manifest: header reads v73; its own inventory row for itself reads v49; the Tracker reads v70. Three values.

201 DDR: file header reads v1.35 while BOTH the Manifest and the Tracker claim v1.37. Either the header is stale after surgical edits, or the file itself is an older version. Nobody can tell which from inside the repository.

AB-CM-029, approved by John 2026-08-11, states the current authoritative DDR is v1.37 and explicitly names v1.23, v1.26, v1.27, v1.29, v1.33 and v1.35 as superseded. The DDR file header reading v1.35 is therefore a STALE HEADER, not an older file — the exact ambiguity that could not be settled from inside the repository. carriedForward.subject: Compatibility-level trap: Azure SQL Database is AHEAD of the local instance on regex
carriedForward.status: ACCEPTED 2026-08-24 — recorded with a re-evaluation trigger; no check built, no upgrade performed
carriedForward.what: REGEXP_LIKE, REGEXP_MATCHES and REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE require database compatibility level 170+. Level 170 is SQL Server 2025 (17.x). The owner's local instance is SQL Server 2022, 16.0.1190.2 — maximum compatibility level 160. These functions are GENERALLY AVAILABLE in Azure SQL Database and UNAVAILABLE locally.
carriedForward.whyItMatters: This is the INVERSE of the FR-010 problem. FR-010 catches 'works locally, fails on Azure', because Developer Edition is more permissive. This is 'works on Azure, fails locally'. FR-010 does not cover it and correctly should not — its objective is Azure compatibility. Both directions produce a green result in one environment and a broken one in the other.
carriedForward.notActedOnBecause: No DDL exists. Nothing can violate it yet. It should be known before the first script is written.
options: Accept and rely on CI, which runs against neither environment today
Add a companion check for local-unavailable constructs
Raise the local instance to SQL Server 2025 so both environments share a capability floor
carriedForward.relatedFinding: Fuzzy string-matching in Azure SQL Database is PREVIEW, not GA. Adopting a preview feature would repeat the free-threaded-Python pattern the guide already prohibits in section 6. It is also unregistered, therefore DENIED by default under the technology registry.
carriedForward.decision: Owner accepted the risk. Rationale: the affected construct set is tiny, and it fails LOUDLY and IMMEDIATELY on first local execution — the opposite of the FR-010 failure mode, where Developer Edition runs everything happily and the failure surfaces at deployment. Building a check for a defect that announces itself spends effort on the wrong risk. Upgrading the local instance was rejected for now because OQ-13 is open: if Managed Instance is chosen the version story changes, and the work might be redone.
carriedForward.reEvaluationTrigger: Re-evaluate at whichever comes FIRST: (a) the first DDL is written, or (b) OQ-13 resolves. Both are real events, not 'someday'.
carriedForward.durableAnswer: The regex case is one instance of a general divergence: Azure SQL Database tracks ahead of the boxed product, so any post-2022 capability may exist in the target and not locally. ddrVersionFinding.finding: THE DDR FILE IS GENUINELY v1.35. Versions 1.36 and 1.37 were never written.
evidence: DDR changelog's HIGHEST entry is 1.35. No 1.36 entry. No 1.37 entry. Header and changelog agree independently.
'1.36' appears NOWHERE in any project document.
'v1.37' appears only as a POINTER in 402 and 403 — never as a changelog entry.

402 line 374 states 'CR-5 item 3 widened in the DDR (v1.37) to include data-availability'. The DDR contains ZERO occurrences of 'data-availability', and still says CR-5 item 3 'still has no storage home'.
SELECTIVE MISS CONFIRMED: the same batch (B2.8, 2026-08-04) claimed edits to 301 and the DDR. 301 got its change — 'required_inputs' appears 25 times. The DDR did not.
ddrVersionFinding.likeliestReading: The 301 tagging landed. The DDR clause described what that tagging IMPLIES for CR-5 item 3 rather than recording an applied DDR edit, and '(v1.37)' was written as the version the DDR WOULD carry. The pointer then stuck and propagated.
ddrVersionFinding.compromisedArtifact: AB-CM-029 is an APPROVED overlay instructing that pointers be corrected TO v1.37. Executing it propagates a version that was never written. Approved, embedded in the repository in five places, premise unsupported.
ddrVersionFinding.propagation: 402 line 389 shows a v1.33 pointer being actively 'corrected' UP to v1.37 — cementing the phantom.
ddrVersionFinding.residualUncertainty: ONE claimed 1.36/1.37 change was tested. Other claimed changes may exist that were not found. One checked claim is not a proof.
ddrVersionFinding.doNotDo: Do NOT set the DDR version to 1.37. The version label must follow the content decision, not precede it.
ownerDecisionsRequired: Was the CR-5 item 3 widening to data-availability ever actually DECIDED, or only planned?
Should the DDR advance to 1.36 with that change applied, or remain at 1.35 with the Tracker and Manifest corrected DOWNWARD?
ddrVersionFinding.agentErrorRecorded: The agent earlier asserted the header was stale and the file current, taking AB-CM-029's word rather than opening the changelog. Third occasion this session where reading the source contradicted a confident summary. The correction came from checking, not from being challenged.
